data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism ends with a sweeping, unsupported universal empirical assertion: 'Unlike every previously studied system of this kind, which faced identical structural constraints yet exhibited none of this behaviour.' This claim (1) is presented without any premise, derivation, or reference — the premises array and derivation array are both empty — yet it asserts exhaustive knowledge about 'every previously studied system'; (2) appears factually false, since rule-based accounts that separate rationality from outcome-expectation are a well-known, widely studied pattern (e.g., deontological ethics, rule-utilitarianism, Popperian falsificationism itself as traditionally understood), so it is not true that no previously studied system exhibited this behaviour; and (3) is doing hidden load-bearing work: without the comparative contrast, the mechanism collapses into a mere restatement of the claim rather than a justification. A conjecture whose only support is an unevidenced universal that is also false does not constitute a defensible target.
